subject: Mathematics
sourceFile: Core Subjects -- GENERAL MATHEMATICS OR MATHEMATICS (CORE).txt
examFormat: Two papers, both of which must be taken. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice objective questions drawn from the common areas of the syllabus, answered in 1 1/2 hours for 50 marks. Paper 2: thirteen essay questions in Sections A and B, answered in 2 1/2 hours for 100 marks, with ten questions answered in all. Section A has five compulsory elementary questions (40 marks); Section B has eight longer questions of which five are answered (60 marks), with a maximum of two drawn from parts of the syllabus that may not be peculiar to candidates' home countries.
excluded: Nothing excluded: the syllabus has no country split (some topics carry symbols in the source, apparently marking Section B-only items, which are included). Aims, units, calculator and equipment notes were skipped.

subtopics.name: Number Bases
objectives: Convert numbers from one base to another, including conversion to and from base 10
Perform addition, subtraction and multiplication of numbers in different bases

subtopics.name: Modular Arithmetic
objectives: Explain the concept of modulo arithmetic and interpret statements such as 6 + 4 = k (mod 7)
Perform addition, subtraction and multiplication in modulo arithmetic
Apply modulo arithmetic to daily life, e.g. market days, clock, shift duty

subtopics.name: Fractions, Decimals and Approximations
objectives: Perform basic operations on fractions and decimals
Give approximations and significant figures, using realistic approximations

subtopics.name: Indices
objectives: State and apply the laws of indices, including simple negative and fractional indices
Express large and small numbers in standard form (scientific notation)

subtopics.name: Logarithms
objectives: Relate indices and logarithms, e.g. y = 10^k implies log10 y = k
State and apply the basic rules of logarithms
Use tables of logarithms and antilogarithms in calculations involving multiplication, division, powers and roots

subtopics.name: Sequence and Series
objectives: Recognise patterns of sequences and determine any term of a given sequence
Solve simple cases of arithmetic progression (A.P.) and geometric progression (G.P.), including word problems (include the sum for A.P. and exclude the sum for G.P.)

subtopics.name: Sets
objectives: Explain the idea of sets: universal sets, finite and infinite sets, subsets, empty sets and disjoint sets
Use the notation and properties of union, intersection and complement (commutative, associative, distributive)
Solve practical problems involving classification using Venn diagrams (at most 3 sets)

subtopics.name: Logical Reasoning
objectives: Identify simple statements, true and false statements, negation and implications
Use the symbols for implication and Venn diagrams in logical reasoning

subtopics.name: Positive and Negative Integers, Rational Numbers
objectives: Perform the four basic operations on rational numbers
Match rational numbers with points on the number line
Use the notation for natural numbers (N), integers (Z) and rational numbers (Q)

subtopics.name: Surds (Radicals)
objectives: Simplify and rationalise simple surds of the forms sqrt(b), a sqrt(b) and a +/- sqrt(b), where a is rational and b is a positive integer
Perform basic operations on surds

subtopics.name: Matrices and Determinants
objectives: Identify the order, notation and types of matrices (not more than 3 x 3)
Add, subtract, multiply by a scalar and multiply matrices
Find the determinant of a 2 x 2 matrix
Apply determinants to solving simultaneous linear equations in two variables

subtopics.name: Ratio, Proportions and Rates
objectives: Find the ratio between two similar quantities and the proportion between two or more similar quantities
Solve problems on financial partnerships, rates of work, costs, taxes (e.g. VAT, withholding tax), foreign exchange, density, mass, distance, time and speed, relating them to real life

subtopics.name: Percentages
objectives: Solve problems on simple interest, commission, discount, depreciation, profit and loss, compound interest (maximum of 3 years), hire purchase and percentage error

subtopics.name: Financial Arithmetic
objectives: Define depreciation and amortization and calculate depreciation on fixed assets and amortization on capitalized assets
Define annuities and solve simple problems on annuities
Describe capital market instruments (shares/stocks, debentures, bonds) and solve simple problems on interest on bonds and debentures

subtopics.name: Variation
objectives: Solve problems on direct, inverse, partial and joint variations
Express variations in mathematical symbols and apply to simple practical problems

subtopics.name: Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Formulate algebraic expressions from given situations
Evaluate algebraic expressions

subtopics.name: Simple Operations on Algebraic Expressions
objectives: Expand expressions, e.g. (a + b)(c + d)
Factorise expressions of the form ax + ay, a(b + c) + d(b + c), a^2 - b^2 and ax^2 + bx + c where a, b, c are integers, and apply the difference of two squares
Carry out binary operations on real numbers, e.g. a*b = 2a + b - ab

subtopics.name: Solution of Linear Equations
objectives: Solve linear equations in one variable and find the truth set
Solve simultaneous linear equations in two variables by elimination, substitution and graphical methods, including word problems

subtopics.name: Change of Subject of a Formula/Relation
objectives: Change the subject of a formula or relation
Substitute values to find the value of a variable

subtopics.name: Quadratic Equations
objectives: Solve quadratic equations by factorization, by completing the square and by formula
Form a quadratic equation with given roots (simple rational roots)
Apply quadratic equations to practical problems

subtopics.name: Graphs of Linear and Quadratic Functions
objectives: Interpret graphs, coordinates of points and tables of values; draw quadratic graphs and obtain roots from graphs
Find coordinates of maximum and minimum points, intercepts on the axes and the axis of symmetry, and recognise sketched graphs
Solve graphically a pair of equations of the form y = ax^2 + bx + c and y = mx + k, and use quadratic graphs to solve related equations
Draw tangents to curves to determine the gradient at a given point

subtopics.name: Linear Inequalities
objectives: Solve linear inequalities in one variable, represent them on the number line and state the truth set
Solve linear inequalities in two variables graphically, and simultaneous linear inequalities graphically
Find maximum and minimum values and apply to real life, e.g. minimum cost, maximum profit and linear programming

subtopics.name: Algebraic Fractions
objectives: Perform operations on algebraic fractions with monomial and binomial denominators (simple cases)
State values for which a fraction is undefined

subtopics.name: Functions and Relations
objectives: Identify types of functions: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many
Describe a function as a mapping and determine the rule of a given mapping/function

subtopics.name: Lengths and Perimeters
objectives: Use Pythagoras theorem and the sine and cosine rules to determine lengths and distances (no formal proofs required)
Calculate lengths of arcs of circles and perimeters of sectors and segments
Calculate distances along latitudes and longitudes and their corresponding angles

subtopics.name: Areas
objectives: Find areas of triangles (including 1/2 base x height and 1/2 ab sin C) and special quadrilaterals: rectangles, parallelograms and trapeziums, areas of similar figures and compound shapes
Find areas of circles, sectors and segments of circles
Find surface areas of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, pyramids, right triangular prisms, cones and spheres, and relate the sector of a circle to the surface area of a cone

subtopics.name: Volumes
objectives: Find volumes of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, right pyramids and spheres, including compound shapes
Find volumes of similar solids

subtopics.name: Angles
objectives: State that angles at a point add up to 360 degrees, adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary and vertically opposite angles are equal
Use acute, obtuse and reflex angles; the degree as a unit of measure

subtopics.name: Angles and Intercepts on Parallel Lines
objectives: Use alternate, corresponding and interior opposite angles on parallel lines
Apply the intercept theorem to proportional division of a line segment

subtopics.name: Triangles and Polygons
objectives: State the angle sum of a triangle and the exterior angle property
Use congruent triangles (conditions SSS, SAS, etc.) and properties of special triangles and special quadrilaterals
Use properties of similar triangles (equiangular properties and ratios of sides and areas)
Use the sum of the angles of a polygon, (n - 2)180 degrees, and the property of exterior angles
Use the fact that parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area

subtopics.name: Circles
objectives: Use properties of chords, including perpendicular bisectors of chords
State and use the angle at the centre being twice the angle at the circumference, the right angle in a semicircle, equal angles in the same segment and supplementary angles in opposite segments
Use the perpendicularity of tangent and radius and the alternate segment theorem

subtopics.name: Construction
objectives: Construct bisectors of angles and line segments, and lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line
Construct angles such as 90, 60, 45, 30 degrees, an angle equal to a given angle and combinations such as 75, 105, 135 degrees
Construct triangles and quadrilaterals from sufficient data

subtopics.name: Loci
objectives: Determine the loci of points at a given distance from a given point or straight line, equidistant from two given points and equidistant from two given straight lines, and their intersections in 2 dimensions

topics.name: Coordinate Geometry of Straight Lines
objectives: Explain the concept of the x-y plane and coordinates of points on it
Find the midpoint of two points and the distance between two points
Find the gradient (slope) of a line
Find the equation of a line in the forms y = mx + c and y - y1 = m(x - x1)

subtopics.name: Sine, Cosine and Tangent of an Angle
objectives: Find the sine, cosine and tangent of acute angles using right-angled triangles and tables of trigonometric ratios
Find the trigonometric ratios of 30, 45 and 60 degrees without tables
Find the sine, cosine and tangent of angles from 0 to 360 degrees, relating to the unit circle
Draw graphs of sine, cosine and other trigonometric ratios, e.g. y = a sin x, y = b cos x, including simultaneous linear and trigonometric equations

subtopics.name: Angles of Elevation and Depression
objectives: Calculate angles of elevation and depression
Apply them to heights and distances (simple problems only)

subtopics.name: Bearings
objectives: Find the bearing of one point from another, using notation such as 035 degrees and N35E
Calculate distances and angles (simple problems; use of diagram required; sine and cosine rules may be used)

topics.name: Introductory Calculus
objectives: Explain the concept of differentiation/derived function and the relationship between the gradient of a curve at a point and the differential coefficient at that point
Differentiate algebraic functions using standard derivatives, e.g. if y = x^2, dy/dx = 2x, and apply to velocity and distance
Apply differentiation to real life situations such as maximum and minimum values and rates of change
Explain the meaning of integration and evaluate simple definite integrals of algebraic functions

subtopics.name: Statistics
objectives: Construct frequency distribution tables and explain class intervals, class mark and class boundary
Draw and interpret pie charts, bar charts, histograms and frequency polygons (excluding unequal class intervals)
Calculate the mean, median and mode for discrete and grouped data (use of an assumed mean acceptable)
Draw and use the cumulative frequency curve (ogive) to estimate the median, quartiles and percentiles
Calculate measures of dispersion: range, semi inter-quartile/inter-quartile range, variance, mean deviation and standard deviation, including standard deviation of grouped data

subtopics.name: Probability
objectives: Distinguish experimental and theoretical probability, including equally likely events
Add probabilities for mutually exclusive and independent events, with and without replacement
Multiply probabilities for independent events, interpreting "and" and "or"

subtopics.name: Vectors in a Plane
objectives: Represent vectors as directed line segments and as Cartesian components
Find the magnitude of a vector and identify equal, zero and parallel vectors
Add and subtract vectors and multiply a vector by a scalar

subtopics.name: Transformation in the Cartesian Plane
objectives: Reflect points and shapes in the x and y axes and in the lines x = k, y = x and y = kx, and determine mirror lines
Rotate points and shapes about the origin and about a point other than the origin, and determine the angle of rotation (-180 to 180 degrees)
Translate points and shapes using a translation vector
Draw images of plane figures under enlargement with a given centre and scale factor
